English: Steam Pit
A primitive pit lined with stones, covered with animal hides and heated by a campfire, used by the tribe for steam cleansing and basic hygiene.
Hot Stone Hut
A small, makeshift wooden hut with a central fire and hot stones, offering warmth and a rudimentary bathing space for nomads.
Smoke Sauna
A partially sunken log structure with a smoke vent and stone benches, filled with aromatic birch smoke for both cleansing and ritual.
Birch Switch Room
A more refined wooden bathhouse, with birch switches for traditional cleansing rituals, increasing the health and unity of the clan.
Wooden Bath Pavilion
A solid log pavilion with benches, heated stones, and a separate cooling area, serving as a social nexus for larger gatherings.
Family Banya
A large, multi-room bathhouse designed for extended families to gather and bathe together, fostering strong kinship bonds.
Community Bathhouse
An imposing central bathhouse for the entire clan, with several heated chambers and communal spaces for feasting and negotiation.
Warmed Hall
A fortified and well-ventilated hall, heated by advanced stone ovens, serving as a center for both hygiene and assembly during harsh winters.
Heated Pavilion
An opulent, multi-chambered wooden structure with intricate heating channels and bathing pools, reserved for the elite and dignitaries.
Grand Slavic Banya
A legendary bathhouse complex built of hewn timber and stone, with vast halls, ritual chambers, and healing pools—a symbol of unity, health, and prosperity for the entire clan.
